statement: By the time a07 ran, arc-03 and f03 had already implemented most of the a07 workpack's checklist without a07 existing yet: typed EffectiveConfig/ProjectConfig structs deriving Deserialize (model.rs, project_tie.rs, policy.rs), deny_unknown_fields on the non-flattened structs (project_tie.rs, policy.rs), fail-closed ConfigLoadError naming the source path (resolve.rs, project_tie.rs), and RuleId (not String) as the map key type for policy.rule_toggles. The only genuinely missing piece was the env.rs module: enforcer-config had zero std::env reads anywhere.
why: The a07 workpack was authored against an earlier crate layout (before arc-03/f03 landed) and named load.rs/env.rs/schema.rs as its owned files, but the crate that actually exists put load logic in lib.rs and schema logic split across model.rs/project_tie.rs/policy.rs. Blindly creating load.rs and schema.rs per the workpack text would have duplicated arc-03/f03's already-correct implementations.
howToApply: When a workpack's 'owns' file list predates a crate that already exists, read the whole existing crate first and diff the workpack's acceptance checklist against it line by line before writing any code. For each checklist item already satisfied, add a pinning test citing the existing implementation instead of new impl code; only write new code for genuinely absent items.

statement: Added crates/enforcer-config/src/env.rs as the sole std::env reader for this crate, declaring exactly two typed vars (ENFORCER_CONFIG_PATH: Option<PathBuf>, ENFORCER_PROFILE: Option<String> validated against KNOWN_PROFILE_NAMES). Both use an injectable EnvLookup trait (ProcessEnv for real reads, FakeEnv in tests) instead of std::env::set_var/remove_var races. A new ConfigLoadError::InvalidEnvVar variant makes a bad ENFORCER_PROFILE value a typed, fail-closed error rather than a silent fallback to the file's own profileName.
why: The workpack requires env.rs to 'declare each consumed var, its type, and required/default, and fail-closed on unknown/missing-required.' There was no existing precedent inside enforcer-config to extend, and no other crate's env-var names overlap these two, so this was additive rather than a rewrite of anything.
howToApply: Any future addition to enforcer-config's env surface must go through env.rs's ConfigEnv struct, not a scattered std::env::var call; add the var name as a const, extend ConfigEnv's fields, and decode it inside read_from with a fail-closed match arm.

statement: EffectiveConfig's field-group structs (ShapeOwnershipGlobs, RuntimeLiteralPolicy, CargoDependencyPolicy, RustScanScope) intentionally omit #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] even though sibling structs in the same crate (project_tie.rs, policy.rs) use it. This is because EffectiveConfig flattens all four groups into one struct via #[serde(flatten)], and serde's flatten + deny_unknown_fields combination does not work reliably (flatten's catch-all Value swallows what would otherwise be an unknown-field error). This is a real serde constraint, not an oversight arc-03 left behind.
why: a07's checklist calls for deny_unknown_fields 'where appropriate' on the schema surface; the qualifier matters here because blindly adding it to the flattened structs would either fail to compile as intended or silently not enforce what it appears to enforce.
howToApply: Before adding deny_unknown_fields to a struct, check whether it (or its parent) is ever deserialized via #[serde(flatten)] anywhere in the crate; if so, either skip deny_unknown_fields on that struct or restructure so validation happens post-flatten (e.g. the cover-all completeness test in lib.rs's proof_fixtures module, which asserts every raw JSON key maps to a typed field via a different mechanism).

statement: Env-var tests that mutate the real process environment (std::env::set_var/remove_var) are racy under cargo test's default parallel-threaded execution if two tests in the same binary touch the same var name. a07 avoided this for the pure-decode logic by threading an EnvLookup trait through ConfigEnv::read_from and using a FakeEnv in unit tests (env.rs), reserving the 3 real-std::env integration tests (lib.rs env_integration_tests module) for proving end-to-end wiring only, each with its own Drop-guarded var cleanup.
why: Needed both: fast, deterministic, parallel-safe coverage of the decode logic itself, AND at least minimal proof that load_project_config_with_env actually reads the real process environment (a fake-only test suite could pass while the real wiring was broken, e.g. a typo'd var name string).
howToApply: When a crate needs to test std::env-dependent code, split into (1) an injectable-lookup trait tested exhaustively with a fake in the crate's normal unit tests, and (2) a small number of real-std::env integration tests with RAII guards (impl Drop { std::env::remove_var }) that only prove the wiring, not the decode edge cases.
